wy_circus_wall.blurb: Circus Wall is a compact sport crag in the lower part of Ten Sleep Canyon, tucked into a narrow cleft that sits uphill from the Ice Plant sector. It holds 14 bolted routes, with the bulk at 5.11 and a handful of 5.12s, plus one 5.13 and a pair of easier lines at 5.8 and 5.9. A few of the lines here are rated among the best in the canyon. The setting feels secluded and gets a different sun and shade pattern than much of the rest of Ten Sleep, so it suits climbers who already have some 5.11 mileage.

wy_grasshopper_wall_the.blurb: The Grasshopper Wall is a steep sport wall in the French Cattle Ranch zone of Ten Sleep Canyon, at roughly 8,000 feet. The stone is very hard and striped in blue, black, grey and gold, with tiny edges, knobs and pockets, so footwork and finger strength matter more than anything else. Of its 14 bolted routes, half sit at 5.13, with the rest scattered between 5.9 and 5.12. Lines run roughly 80 to 120 feet. The wall faces mostly southeast and catches sun through the morning into early afternoon. It is a hard-climber's wall; few routes here are suited to beginners.

wy_hoodoos_the.blurb: The Hoodoos are a jumble of big pale travertine blocks that slid off Terrace Mountain, just south of Mammoth Hot Springs in Yellowstone National Park. Climbing here is a small-scale affair: eight boulder problems from V1 to about V6, mostly V3 to V4, along with six top-rope lines on the faces that run from 5.5 to 5.10. Travertine is unusual stone to climb on and has a feel of its own. It is a short stop for a couple of hours rather than a full-day destination.

wy_middle_teton.blurb: Middle Teton rises to about 12,800 feet in Grand Teton National Park, the third-highest summit in the range. It is a quieter peak than its neighbor the Grand Teton, and most approaches start from the Lupine Meadows trailhead and climb through Garnet Canyon, a day of roughly 6,000 feet of gain. The 14 listed climbs are alpine ridges, snow and ice couloirs and a few steep rock lines, from easy scrambling and Class 4 up to 5.7 ridges and one very hard 5.13 wall. The standard Southwest Couloir is a scramble rather than a roped climb. Late summer is the usual window, once snow has melted back.

wy_crystal_freeway.blurb: At Vedauwoo, Crystal Freeway is the northern side of Friction Tower, reached along the Box Canyon trail and across the saddle beside Turtle Rock. The face is a broad, upturned granite slab speckled with feldspar crystals that serve as small holds for technical footwork, while the cracks beside it are sharp enough that tape is worth packing. Of its 13 routes, most are trad and two are bolted. They run from an easy 5.2 through plenty of 5.6 to 5.9 terrain up to a few 5.11s and one 5.12. The slab is usually sunny. Vedauwoo is busy on weekends, so weekdays are quieter.

wy_lower_psychoactive.blurb: Lower Psychoactive is a sport sector in Leigh Creek canyon near Ten Sleep, below the Upper Psychoactive wall. The climbs here tend to be fairly short and lower in angle, with technical movement. Its 13 bolted routes are split between a few easy lines in the 5.6 to 5.7 range, a single 5.9, and a solid block of 5.11s, topping out with a couple of 5.12s and one 5.13. A creek crossing is part of the walk in, which can be running high early in the season. It suits climbers working in the 5.11 range.

wy_grand_parade.blurb: Grand Parade is one of the sub-sectors of the Dry Wall in lower Ten Sleep Canyon, below the switchback. This part of the wall is known for cracks, some of them sharp. It has 13 routes, eleven bolted and two on gear, with the grades clustered at 5.10 to 5.12 and only a single 5.9 for those wanting something easier. The Dry Wall as a whole picks up sun early and falls into shade by mid-afternoon, which makes it handy for summer evenings and winter mornings. The walk from the road is short.
